items.title: Art Futures Camp 2026 – Diriyah Art Futures
items.content_text: Art Futures Summer Camp for Arabic-Speaking Teens is a three-week immersive programme hosted by Diriyah Art Futures (DAF), the MENA region’s first centre dedicated to New Media Arts. Designed for Arabic-speaking teens aged 14–18, the camp offers an in-depth introduction to digital art practices in a dynamic and supportive environment. Under the 2026 theme, “Digital Art and Portraiture,” participants explore new ways of representing identity in the digital age, questioning how individuals are portrayed when faces become data and images circulate beyond physical presence. The programme combines creative experimentation with foundational technical skills, including Fab Lab practices and digital studio portraiture. Throughout the camp, participants work closely with industry specialists and creative mentors, culminating in a collaborative exhibition produced with DAF’s curatorial and exhibition teams to showcase their work. Applications are officially open, with aspiring young creatives in Riyadh able to apply until Sunday, June 7.

items.title: البرنامج الصيفي بجامعة الجوف 2026
items.content_text: تطلق جامعة الجوف البرنامج الصيفي بجامعة الجوف 1447هـ – 2026م، بوصفه برنامجًا نوعيًا متكاملًا يستهدف تنمية المهارات وتطويرها، ونشر ثقافة الابتكار، وترسيخ ثقافة التطوع وخدمة المجتمع، بما يعزز دور الجامعة التنموي والمجتمعي، ويفتح مسارات واسعة لاستثمار فترة الصيف في برامج معرفية وتدريبية وتطوعية ورياضية موجهة لمنسوبي الجامعة وطلبتها والخريجين وأفراد المجتمع. ويستهدف البرنامج، الذي يمتد من شهر يوليو حتى نهاية أغسطس 2026م، أكثر من 16,000مستفيد من داخل الجامعة وخارجها، من خلال أكثر من 50 برنامجًا وفعالية نوعية، وما يزيد على 210 ساعة تدريبية مكثفة، إلى جانب مشاركة أكثر من 300 متطوع أكاديمي وطبي، وتنفيذ أكثر من 11,000 ساعة تطوعية معتمدة، إضافة إلى أكثر من 10 بطولات رياضية صيفية.

items.title: Zoom In
items.content_text: A tiny fragment holds the clue. In this Praise of the Artisan treasure hunt, children begin with a zoomed-in detail taken from a larger artwork, a pattern, texture, or small visual hint. Moving through the space, they search for the full piece, matching what they see up close with what appears on the walls. As the search unfolds, attention shifts to details that are often overlooked, building observation skills through careful looking. Each match reveals the complete artwork behind the fragment.

items.title: Mishkat Summer Camp
items.content_text: Discover the exciting world of science, energy, and innovation at Mishkat Summer Camp 2026, where young learners can explore the future through hands-on experiments, interactive challenges, educational games, and collaborative activities designed to inspire curiosity, creativity, and teamwork. Organised by Mishkat Interactive Center, an initiative of the King Abdullah City for Atomic and Renewable Energy (K.A.CARE), the camp introduces participants to the future of energy while developing STEAM skills through experiential learning. Activities explore topics such as solar, wind, and nuclear energy, hydrogen technologies, the circular carbon economy, artificial intelligence, innovation, and programming, supporting Saudi Vision 2030's goals of building future-ready generations. items.title: Wrth Summer Art & Craft Program
items.content_text: Introduce your children to the richness of Saudi Arabia's traditional arts at the Wrth Summer Art & Craft Program 2026, organized by the Royal Institute of Traditional Arts (Wrth). Taking place at Riyadh Park from 16 to 18 July 2026, the program offers children aged 8–12 an enriching summer experience through a sensory, hands-on journey exploring the traditional arts of the Kingdom's diverse regions. Through a variety of interactive activity stations, children will discover heritage-inspired crafts including pottery, Al Sadu weaving, traditional incense burner (mabkharah) making, Najdi door decoration, and other traditional art forms. Designed to nurture creativity, develop practical skills, and deepen appreciation for Saudi culture, the program provides an engaging environment where young learners can explore, create, and connect with the Kingdom's rich artistic heritage. items.content_text: Producers have a strong intuition that allows them to uncover hidden stories and present them in a cohesive, professional, and engaging way. Production isn’t just a job; it’s a lifestyle and a mindset. items.content_text: Saudi Food Manufacturing returns to Riyadh as the Kingdom’s hub for next-generation food technology, automation, and global partnerships supporting industrial growth and Vision 2030 economic diversification. Alongside the exhibition, the Food Forward Summit features expert-led insights on innovation economics, greener production, and smarter manufacturing, while the “Get Connected” B2B programme matches exhibitors with selected factory owners and top buyers for focused, high-value meetings on the show floor. items.content_text: Hotel & Hospitality Expo Saudi Arabia takes place in Riyadh from 13–15 September 2026 at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, bringing together leading local and international brands with some of the Kingdom’s most influential buyers across the hotel and hospitality sector. As Saudi Arabia’s tourism and travel growth accelerates in line with Vision 2030, the expo offers a prime platform to build partnerships, discover the latest trends and technologies, and connect with global exhibitors and designers. items.title: Saudi International Falcons & Hunting Exhibition
items.content_text: The Saudi International Falcons and Hunting Exhibition is one of the largest events dedicated to falconry and hunting in Saudi and globally. It brings together everything related to falconry and outdoor excursions, from falcons and hunting tools to equipment and gear associated with hunting trips, all within a comprehensive space that allows visitors to explore this field in one place. The exhibition also features platforms showcasing a wide range of brands, alongside accompanying activities and events suitable for families, creating an experience that blends cultural and entertainment elements. The event plays an important role in preserving falconry heritage and raising awareness by offering content that introduces visitors to its history and significance within Saudi’s cultural identity.

items.title: Making Short Films
items.content_text: Filmmakers, photographers, cinematographers and actors are welcomed to join us for a seven-day filmmaking course under the supervision of Jaan Al-Balushi. Nearly 20 participants will come to Ithra every day from 4 to 9 p.m. to cover the stages of filmmaking, starting from the idea and scriptwriting, filming, and, finally, to editing. Editing equipment, such as the Adobe Premiere software, will be available. At the end of the course, three individual teams will each produce a short film ranging between two to seven minutes.
